evidence:
host/native/pull-service.lisp:284-293 (fnn-pull-local-send)
                 (loop
                   (multiple-value-bind (octets rest donep yieldedp)
                       (fnn-owner-render-next-quantum service cid plan :transit)
                     (setq reply (concatenate 'fnn-octets reply octets))
                     ...
            (setq pending (subseq pending consumed))

host/native/web-host.lisp:116-127 (fnn-web-feed): same loop, (setq reply (concatenate 'fnn-octets reply part)), then (fnn-web-fill in reply).
The pull caller then makes an octet list of the whole reply: (enqueue (cons :local (fnn-octet-list reply))) at pull-service.lisp:409.
fix: Stream the windows. Hand each rendered window to the consumer as it is produced (the pull session as a :local event per window; the web session into fn-web-in as an append bounded by ACL2's page limit). Track an offset into pending instead of re-subseqing it.
reviewer: pull-service.lisp:288 and web-host.lisp:119 both run (setq reply (concatenate 'fnn-octets reply part)) once per render window, which is O(W^2) copying with the whole reply resident. pull-service.lisp:409 then converts the whole reply to an octet list. (subseq pending consumed) per step is quadratic in the number of pipelined lines. The cost is bounded by reply size: pull-path local replies are mostly status lines to commands ACL2 issues, and web commands are ACL2-built under the web limits. So this is a real D27 representation and efficiency defect with modest practical impact.
scenario: The render plan is windowed precisely so that a reply is never materialized at once (D27: bound work and allocation per step). These two callers undo that. A web page that sends OVER or LISTGROUP for a large group, or an ARTICLE near the profile bound, renders W windows and copies O(W^2 * window) octets, keeping the whole reply resident. On the pull path the whole reply is then turned into a cons list (about 16 bytes per octet). The reply size depends on the store and the peer's commands, not on any per-step bound. `(subseq pending consumed)` per step is likewise quadratic in the number of lines in a large pipelined input.
title: Pull-feed and web replies are built whole by repeated concatenate: quadratic copying and whole-reply allocation per request
